title: KV Cache Architecture - v3 (shards, eviction, pools, fragmentation)
content:
Summary:

This doc is a working draft of the KV cache architecture for the serving runtime (v3). Focus areas: memory layout, allocation pools, eviction strategies, fragmentation mitigation and defrag/compaction approaches, and operational tradeoffs. This iteration consolidates learnings from v1/v2 experiments and runtime profiling on 16G/40G GPU hosts.

Goals:
- Provide a high-throughput, low-latency KV cache for KV-cache lookups used by autoregressive decoding (per-request KV caches + shared prefix cache).
- Keep tail latency predictable under mixed-model workloads and wide sequence-length distribution.
- Limit memory fragmentation and enable predictable GC/compaction windows to avoid latency spikes.
- Allow dynamic memory accounting per-customer/tenant for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Constraints:
- Typical key sizes vary from 64B (small KV entries) up to 2MB (large cached KV blobs for long contexts).
- GPUs have limited device memory; host RAM used as overflow for cold entries.
- Concurrency: thousands of concurrent requests with hot prefixes reused across requests.
- Need for graceful eviction and seamless fallback to smaller model variants or recompute.

High-level architecture:
- Sharded in-memory KV cache. Sharding by key-hash (power-of-two shards) to enable parallel allocation/eviction and reduce lock contention. Default shards = #CPU-cores / 2 (min 16).
- Each shard manages multiple memory pools (slab-style for size classes + a large-object arena).
- Two-layer residency: GPU-resident hot pool (optional, when running with GPU-backed KV) + host RAM warm pool + on-disk cold store (optional; used for Dedicated/Private).
- Metadata (index) is a compact shard-local hash table with atomic pointers to entries and epoch counters for safe concurrent updates.

Memory layout and allocation:
- Size classes: power-of-two buckets from 64B up to 256KB. Allocations <= 256KB use slab allocator per-shard/size-class. >256KB go to large-object arena which uses a buddy allocator to reduce fragmentation.
- Slab pages are contiguous blocks (default 4MB) split into fixed-size frames. Each slab maintains a free-list (lock-free or shard-lock guarded depending on contention). Slabs are tracked as hot/neutral/cold based on access frequency.
- Large-object arena: contiguous pages (min 1MB) allocated via mmap on host and optional pin-to-GPU pipeline for GPU residency. Allocation headers for arena blocks include: size, timestamp, last-access, reference count, and a generation tag (string id) to enable quick invalidation on model-rollout.
- Metadata and index are kept in a compact form: 8-byte key-hash, 8-byte pointer (shard-local index), 4-byte flags, 4-byte generation/version -> fits into 24 bytes per entry in most cases. Index growth uses incremental rehashing to prevent O(n) pauses.

Pools and residency tiers:
- Hot GPU pool (optional): small-capacity pool pinned in device memory for extremely hot keys (small tokens / KV frames). Admission policy is cost-aware: promote entries by frequency and by estimated downstream cost (recompute cost metric). Eviction is based on segmented-LRU with admission filters to prevent thrashing.
- Warm host RAM pool: main slab allocator and large-object arena live here. Fastest CPU access for majority of lookups.
- Cold on-disk / SSD store: optional for Dedicated/Private deployments where reloading on miss is acceptable. Entries here are stored in compact compressed format and restored asynchronously back to RAM on demand.

Eviction policies and heuristics:
- Multi-tiered eviction. Each shard runs independent eviction to reduce global coordination cost. Tier-specific policies:
  - Hot GPU pool: segmented LRU (S-LRU) with two segments (probation + protected). Promotion on repeated reads. TTL can be applied for entries tied to short-lived requests.
  - Host warm pool: cost-aware LRU (cost = memory_size * predicted_recompute_cost * recent_access_frequency) with decay on frequency over time (exponential decay with half-life configurable).
  - Cold store: manual tier with least-recently-used purge and expiration.
- Eviction should be reactive to memory pressure events and proactive based on admission rate stats. When total usage > watermark_high, evict until usage < watermark_low. Watermarks are per-shard and can be tuned globally.
- Prefer evicting large low-hit entries first (size-aware eviction). But maintain a floor to avoid evicting small critical KV fragments that cause recompute overhead.

Fragmentation handling and compaction:
- Slab allocator reduces fragmentation for small allocations by grouping same-size frames. For large-object arena, fragmentation can occur due to variable sized frees. We use a hybrid: buddy allocator + periodic compaction windows.
- Compaction approach: epoch-based mark-and-compact for arena where candidate blocks are coalesced into new contiguous pages. Steps:
  1) Quiesce allocation for the target shard/arena page (fast path remains available in other shards).
  2) Allocate new pages, copy live objects, update atomic pointers (use generation-tag + atomic swap), fence, then free old pages.
  3) Background thread does copies in small batches to avoid long GC pauses.
- Defragmentation heuristic: trigger when internal fragmentation > 25% for a shard or when average lookup latency for large-object hits exceeds threshold. Compaction budget per-second is configurable to avoid CPU contention.

Concurrency model and consistency:
- Shard-local metadata: per-shard mutex or reader-writer lock for index mutations. Hot-path lookups should be lock-free reads: read pointer+generation, validate, return. If pointer indicates a move/compaction in flight, fallback to slower path that acquires shard lock.
- Updates (insert/evict) use CAS on index slots and increment epoch counters to allow lock-free readers to detect in-flight changes.
- Reference counting for in-use entries to prevent reclamation while requests are reading. Reclamation is deferred to epoch-reclaimer threads.
- Atomic promotion: when promoting to GPU hot pool, use a two-phase install: allocate GPU slot, copy, then CAS index to GPU pointer. Rollback on failure.

Telemetry, metrics and observability:
- Per-shard metrics: hits, misses, evictions, fragmentation_percent, allocation_rate, free_slabs, slab_count, average_lookup_ns, compaction_time_ns, promotion_count, demotion_count.
- Export sampled traces for eviction decisions and compaction operations to correlate latency spikes with GC.
- Alerting thresholds: sustained miss-rate increase > 5% over 10m; fragmentation > 35% for 5m; compaction CPU > 30% for 1m.

Rollout plan and compatibility:
- v3 will be feature-flag gated. Start with host-only (no GPU hot pool) on canary hosts. Monitor memory and tail latency for 48h.
- Add optional GPU hot pool toggle per-deployment after host behavior is stable.
- Backwards compatibility: support reading existing index blobs; version the generation tag and provide migration tool to upgrade index structures incrementally.

Operational concerns and failure modes:
- Risk: compaction-induced latency spikes. Mitigation: limit compaction bandwidth and perform compaction during low-traffic windows.
- Risk: thrash between GPU hot pool and host pool. Mitigation: admission policy + probation window + sampling-based promotion.
- Risk: multi-tenant cross-tenant eviction. Mitigation: per-tenant quotas and hard caps; prefer tenant-weighted eviction.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Finalize size-class cutoffs (current heuristic: <=256KB slab, >256KB arena). Run production trace-driven simulation to validate.
- Evaluate lock-free slab free-list vs shard mutex for typical contention patterns (bench microbench and p99 lookup).
- Is buddy allocator sufficient for large-object arena or should we pursue a best-fit with coalescing?
- Compression: evaluate lightweight compression for cold-store entries to reduce SSD usage (LZ4) and impact on restore latency.

Appendix: data structures (high level)
- ShardIndexEntry := (key_hash: u64, ptr: u64, flags: u32, gen: u32)  // stored compactly
- SlabPage header := (size_class_id, free_count, hot_counter, last_touch_ts)
- LargeObjectHeader := (size, refcount, last_access_ns, gen, checksum)

Notes to reviewers:
- This doc is intentionally prescriptive but leaves several implementation knobs. Please review the eviction math and fragmentation heuristics.
- Link to prior iterations: CONFS-1245 (v1/v2 notes) and profiling results in SRV-1423.
